summary: Provisioning script fails on systems with legacy locale collation (NFKD) causing device-enroll and imaging stall
description:
Issue summary:
Provisioning helper script (setup_local_policies.sh) exits with non-zero when system locale uses legacy Unicode collation normalization (NFKD) or certain non-default LC_CTYPE/LC_COLLATE values. This stops the imaging task sequence mid-run and prevents Intune check-in/enrollment on a subset of repaired devices.

Impact:
- ~8 machines in the last two depot batches failed imaging and never completed Intune enrollment; users received a partially provisioned workstation (local accounts only, no corp certs).
- Blocks fast-redeploy for depot repair queue; increases turnaround time.

Environment:
- Affected devices repros on prod imaging pool in us-east.
- OS: Windows 11 22H2 corporate image (with latest platform patches as of 2026-03-01)
- Provisioning artifact: provisioning-scripts v2026.02.28 (bash + PowerShell wrapper)
- Managed via SCCM task sequence that runs setup_local_policies.sh late in the image.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Boot a test device (Dell Latitude 7440) into SCCM task sequence in the us-east imaging pool.
2) Set system locale environment to one of the affected collations (example repro used: LC_COLLATE="fi_FI@collation=NFKD" exported in cmd before running the script).
3) Allow task sequence to reach the provisioning-scripts step.
4) Observe that setup_local_policies.sh aborts with an encoding/collation exception and the task sequence halts.

Observed logs (excerpt):
- C:\Windows\Temp\provisioning\setup_local_policies.log:
  [2026-03-09 14:07:02] INFO: starting local policy setup
  [2026-03-09 14:07:03] ERROR: fatal: string normalization failed when writing registry key: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\SOFTWARE\\Redwood\\Provision"
  [2026-03-09 14:07:03] ERROR: exit code 1
- SCCM smsts.log shows task sequence step 'Run Command Line' returning 1 and aborting sequence.

Hypothesis and root cause (initial):
- The helper script uses Python 3.9 subprocess invocation and writes UTF-8 strings to the Windows registry using a small C# helper compiled during the build. Under certain LC_COLLATE/LC_CTYPE values the runtime performs Unicode normalization (NFKD) on strings and strips combining characters; combined with our registry write helper's unsupported normalization mode this results in an exception thrown by the helper (System.ArgumentException: Invalid character in registry value).
- This only triggers when a depot-repair process re-applies device-specific locale settings prior to provisioning (we see this on repaired devices that retain OEM locale overrides).

Temporary workaround applied:
- Imaging team added a wrapper to forcibly set LANG and LC_COLLATE to en_US.UTF-8 before running the provisioning step in the task sequence. This is in place for the current depot batch and prevents the failure.

Next steps / planned fix:
- Engineering (Provisioning) to update provisioning-scripts to sanitize locale inputs and coerce strings to NFC normalization before passing to the registry helper. Also update the C# registry writer to accept NormalizationForm variants. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioning-scripts/pull/412
- Imaging ops to roll the temporary LANG/LC_COLLATE wrapper into the standard task sequence until the patch is deployed.
- Confirm fleet-wide by running a small canary set of 20 repaired devices with the patch and removing wrapper after two successful batches.

Owner: Miguel Torres (Provisioning lead)
Estimated ETA for PR review & QA: 2026-03-16

planned_fix: Update provisioning-scripts to normalize strings to NFC before registry writes and harden the C# registry helper to accept multiple normalization forms. Add unit tests for legacy collation inputs. Roll patch through canary imaging pool and remove LANG wrapper after verification.
workaround: Set LANG and LC_COLLATE to en_US.UTF-8 (or remove OEM locale overrides) in SCCM task sequence before invoking provisioning scripts. Imaging Ops to keep wrapper until patch deployed.
